text.p: The mark sank to session lows against its European stablemates in late trade, with the French franc shooting through 3.42 per mark as mark/Paris longs found themselves squeezed out.
"(Mark/Paris) is the one people have been gunning for for the last couple of weeks and they've got themselves a bit too long," said a trader at a German bank here.

Dealers cited talk that a UK corporate had been selling the cross in sizeable amounts every 10 ticks. Players were also wary of shorting francs ahead of the European Union's monetary committee meeting on monetary union on Monday, they said.

The franc had bounded as far as 3.4160/65 per mark by 1413 GMT, up from late Thursday's European level of 3.4214/19 and a far cry from the nearly seven-month low of 3.4315 it hit early yesterday, prompting Bank of France intervention.
But traders and analysts were far from convinced that the beleaguered franc was now in the clear.
"It looks as if (the mark's) got another move on the downside to square the last remaining long positions, and then we're clear to go back up again," said one London-based dealer.
Analysts said worries over the French government's ability to meet the stiff monetary union criteria would also persist.

"I think we could see it all go horribly wrong. The French are already looking for sleight of hand to get the deficit down to their targetted figure," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.

France's government has forecast a total public deficit of four percent of GDP in 1996 and three in 1997, down from five percent in 1995. But the market fears labour and social unrest will upset the drive to meet monetary union targets.
"Whatever the government announces, I'm sure the opposition to a number of their measures will be quite vocal, and that's bound to disturb franc assets," Edmonds said.
France's Finance Minister Jean Arthuis today said the 1997 budget would forecast growth of 2.3 percent, and confirmed that he envisaged 1996 growth of 1.3 percent.
The 1997 budget -- due to be presented to the cabinet on September 18 -- will increase taxes on alcohol and tobacco to help fund the welfare system, Arthuis said.
The Italian lira firmed to 1013.15/50 per mark by 1431 GMT from Thursday's European close of 1017.70/8.00, while the Swedish crown rose to 4.4690/20 from 4.4725/55.
Spain's peseta climbed a little, but its gains were unspectacular as budget jitters took their toll there too.
Spanish markets buzzed with talk, centred on a newspaper story, that the government would use portions of tariffs on regulated sectors to help pay the public deficit.
The Economy Ministry denied the report, which sent shares in sectors such as electricity and gas tumbling.
The peseta was quoted at 84.41/43 per mark by 1444 GMT compared to 84.52/53 in late Europe yesterday.
